title: Degraded Availability for MAI Code 2 in Copilot

updates.body: We are investigating reports of degraded performance for Copilot AI Model Providers

We are experiencing degraded availability for the MAI Code 2 model in Copilot products and IDE surfaces. This is due to an issue with an upstream model provider. While we work with them to resolve the issue, we recommend choosing another model or selecting ‘Copilot Fusion’ to continue using Copilot.

We have been working with the upstream provider and applying mitigations, and are seeing improvement in availability for MAI Code 2 across Copilot products and IDE surfaces.
We will continue monitoring.

raw.name: Investigating degraded experiences across GitHub products

updates.body: We are investigating reports of impacted performance for some GitHub services.
We have identified an issue that impacts Large File Storage (LFS) for a small number of customers. We are working on mitigation.
We're continuing to investigate elevated error rates affecting a small number of customers using Git LFS. We are still assessing mitigation options and will share updates as we learn more.
We've applied a mitigation to fix the issues in Git LFS. We are seeing improvements in telemetry and are monitoring for full recovery.
The degradation has been mitigated. We are monitoring to ensure stability.

On November 25, 2026, between 21:30 UTC and 00:28 UTC, Git Large File Storage (LFS) operations on github.com were degraded. During this time, an average of 2% of Git LFS requests failed, peaking at 4%. Many more requests initially failed but succeeded when Git LFS clients automatically retried them, which caused slower uploads and downloads for affected users. Other Git operations were not affected. This was due to a large volume of automated, unauthenticated traffic that overwhelmed the Git LFS servers in one of our regions, leaving them unable to respond to requests in time.

We mitigated the incident by moving most Git LFS traffic from the affected region to other regions with more capacity. Error rates returned to normal by 00:28 UTC.

We are working to limit the impact of high-volume unauthenticated traffic on Git LFS, and to add capacity in the affected region, to prevent similar disruptions in the future.
